422.body: connection draining enabled on the main proxy. deploys used to kill in-flight queries. now they drain gracefully.
422.title: postgres-main: enable connection draining

423.body: get_product now returns review summaries (average rating, count) inline. The product page made a separate reviews call per product, which was the slowest part of page load. list_products includes the summary from the same fetch. Testing: asserted the reviews service is no longer called on page load.
423.title: catalog: inline review summaries in get_product

424.body: start_refund now writes an audit record for every state transition, not just creation. Disputes about who approved what used to end in shoulder shrugs. RefundsService logs actor, timestamp, and transition, and workflow.py emits them at each step. Testing: walked a full refund lifecycle and asserted the audit trail.
424.title: refunds: audit trail for refund transitions

425.body: PaymentsService now exposes a refund-status endpoint so merchants stop polling the capture endpoint for refund updates!! capture() and refund() are untouched; the new handler reads the same refund records. The endpoint returns status plus timestamps. Testing: covered found, pending, and unknown refund ids.
425.title: payments-api: add refund-status endpoint

434.body: Slow query alerts now page the channel instead of just emailing. emails were ignored for weeks. paging works 🎯
434.title: postgres-payments: page on slow queries

435.body: route() now logs the chosen provider and the reason at debug level, which makes routing behavior auditable for the first time. The logs go to the standard router log group. PaymentRouter performance is unaffected. Testing: confirmed log lines for normal, fallback, and canary decisions.
435.title: payment-router: debug logging for route decisions

436.body: refund() now supports partial refunds against a previous partial: it tracks the refunded total per order and each new request is validated against the remainder. Previously only one partial per order worked and the second failed with a confusing error. PaymentsService keeps the running total and capture() is untouched. Testing: multiple-partial sequences covered.
436.title: payments-api: allow multiple partial refunds

437.body: reserve() now holds stock for 15 minutes instead of 10. Shoppers with slow checkouts kept losing holds at the payment step!! The TTL config drives it, and InventoryService logs the effective hold at debug level. OutOfStock behavior is unchanged. Testing: asserted the new expiry in the reservation tests.
437.title: inventory: extend reservation hold to 15 min

438.body: redis memory alarm threshold set to 80%. was 95%, too late to react. paged twice since, both real 🌱
438.title: redis-cache: lower memory alarm threshold

439.body: dispatch() now adds a request id header if the client didn't send one, so every request is traceable end to end. Half our traffic arrived without ids. Downstream services already propagate it. Testing: asserted the header exists on all responses.
439.title: api-gateway: inject request ids in dispatch

440.body: ledger point-in-time recovery tested end to end. restored to 5 min before a simulated bad migration. worked, documented.
440.title: postgres-ledger: point-in-time recovery test

441.body: test_place_order_confirmation_mentions_order now covers the gift-message variant, which was the only confirmation shape without a test. fresh_state seeds a gift order, place_order handles it as before, and the assertion checks the gift line renders. No production code changed. Testing: the new case plus the full checkout suite.
441.title: checkout: cover gift confirmations in tests

450.body: PaymentRouter now supports a maintenance mode flag that routes everything to the secondary provider during provider maintenance windows. Flipping this used to need a config deploy. __init__ reads the flag, route() honors it, and clear() resets it. Testing: enabled maintenance mode and confirmed zero traffic to the primary.
450.title: payment-router: maintenance-mode routing

451.body: start_refund now validates the order is in a refundable state before creating the refund record. Refunds for already-cancelled orders created zombie records that finance had to void by hand. workflow.py surfaces the validation error to the caller. Testing: covered cancelled, completed, and in-flight orders.
451.title: refunds: validate order state in start_refund

452.body: weekend vacuum full. autovacuum tuned again. logs quiet, tables healthy.
452.title: postgres-payments: weekend vacuum tuning

453.body: login() in oauth.py now retries the provider userinfo call once on transient failure instead of failing the whole login. Provider hiccups caused visible login failures weekly. The retry is a single immediate re-attempt, not a loop. Testing: simulated a failing-then-recovering provider and confirmed login succeeds.
453.title: auth: retry userinfo fetch in oauth login

454.body: test_capture_new_attempt_charges_again documents the current re-attempt behavior with a dedicated case: same order, new attempt, full flow through the handler. The old suite only covered the same-attempt path, so the new-attempt path was effectively untested. refund() coverage in the same file is unchanged, and fresh_state seeds both scenarios. Testing: the new case passes and the full file is green.
454.title: payments-api: cover new-attempt capture in tests

456.body: redis replication lag alarm added. pages when a replica falls behind by more than 10s. tested 📡
456.title: redis-cache: replica lag alarm

457.body: idle session timeout set to 30 min. stale sessions were piling up. cleaned.
457.title: postgres-main: set idle session timeout

458.body: dispatch() now rejects requests with malformed JSON at the gateway with a 400 instead of proxying them to services that each failed differently. One bad client generated five different error shapes. Route matching and check_limit are unchanged. Testing: asserted uniform 400s for malformed bodies.
458.title: api-gateway: reject malformed JSON at gateway

467.body: LedgerEntry now carries a kind field distinguishing payments, refunds, and adjustments. Reporting queries had to infer kind from amount signs, which broke on zero-amount adjustments. FakeBus and publish() pass it through, and old entries read back as 'unknown'. Testing: kind-specific reporting queries covered.
467.title: ledger: add entry kind to LedgerEntry

468.body: post_entry now returns the assigned sequence number so callers can track their entries without a follow-up read. Two services were doing write-then-read just for the number. LedgerEntry assigns it at write time. Testing: asserted the returned number matches the stored one.
468.title: ledger: return sequence number from post_entry

469.body: reserve() now checks the per-SKU reservation cap before writing, rejecting with a clear 'cap reached' result instead of letting one SKU eat the whole reservation table. A flash sale last month starved every other SKU. InventoryService reads the cap from config, and OutOfStock is raised only for genuinely empty stock. Testing: cap-reached and normal-path cases added.
469.title: inventory: per-SKU reservation caps in reserve

470.body: with_retry now emits a metric per attempt with the function name as a label, so the retry dashboard finally has real data instead of estimates. The metric fires alongside the existing logs and MAX_ATTEMPTS behavior is identical. CheckoutService passes the label through. Testing: asserted metric counts match attempt counts in the test scenarios.
470.title: checkout: per-attempt metrics in with_retry

471.body: route() now supports sticky provider selection per merchant: merchants with a pinned provider always route there unless the provider is unhealthy. Two enterprise merchants contractually require a specific provider. PaymentRouter reads pins from config, __init__ validates them, and clear() resets pins. Unpinned traffic is unchanged. Testing: pinned and unpinned flows verified.
471.title: payment-router: sticky provider pins in route

472.body: Hello — login() now shows a specific 'account locked' message with the unlock time instead of a generic failure that sent users to support. AuthService.login computes the message from the lockout record. Successful logins and other failures are unchanged. Testing: covered locked, recently-unlocked, and never-locked accounts.
472.title: auth: clear locked-account message in login

473.body: slow query sampling rate increased. was 1%, missed rare bad queries. now 10%. dashboards updated.
473.title: postgres-payments: increase slow-query sampling

474.body: AuthService.login now warns when the account uses a deprecated password hash and rehashes on next success. A slice of very old accounts still used the legacy scheme. The warning goes to the security log only, users see nothing different. Testing: legacy-hash login rehashes and the warning fires.
474.title: auth: rehash legacy password hashes on login
